events.name: The Trivia Mentor
events.intro: A silver-haired woman sits on a folding stool by the path, a thermos of tea at her feet and a notebook open on her knee, every page full of tiny handwriting about moves. She closes it and folds her hands on top. She: "Answer three questions and I will teach you a move nobody remembers." She looks at your team, one by one, and something in her face softens. She: "Not questions from a book. Questions about you."

success.text: She pours herself a cup of tea and does not offer you one yet. She: "First question, then."
She shrugs and opens the notebook again. She: "The move will still be forgotten tomorrow."

events.name: The Trivia Mentor: The First Question
events.intro: She: "Which of these was with you on the first day?" She waits, the cup halfway to her lips, while your team shuffles in front of her.

branches.text: She looks at the one you chose, then at you, and smiles. She: "Of course. You did not even have to think." She makes a small tick in the notebook.

success.text: She looks at the one you chose for a long moment, then shakes her head gently. She: "Not that one. But you love it like it was." She makes a mark in the notebook.

events.name: The Trivia Mentor: The Second Question
events.intro: She sets the cup down. Her voice goes quieter. She: "Second question. Has anyone in your care fallen on this road, and not got up again?"

branches.text: She nods, and for a moment neither of you says anything. She: "Then you remember them. Good. That is the right answer, though I am sorry it is." A small tick.

success.text: She studies you, and then your team, and shakes her head slowly. She: "No. Not yet. Keep it that way." She does not tick the notebook, but she does not seem to mind.

branches.text: She looks at you a long time, and you look away first. She: "That is not true, and you know it is not." She does not tick the notebook.

success.text: She looks at your team, all of them, and nods. She: "Good. Then you know exactly how many you have." A small tick in the notebook.

events.name: The Trivia Mentor: The Third Question
events.intro: She finishes her tea. She: "Last one. How many Gym badges are in your case?"

branches.text: She taps your bag, where the badge case clinks. She: "Count again." No tick.

success.text: She: "None. Honest. The badges will come." A small tick.

branches.text: She shakes her head. She: "More than that. You have stopped counting." No tick.
She: "Yes. Every one of them earned." A small tick.

success.text: She shakes her head. She: "Count again." No tick.

branches.text: She: "Three or more, and you still remember every Gym." A small tick.

success.text: She shakes her head. She: "Not yet. But you will." No tick.

events.name: The Trivia Mentor: Nobody Remembers It
events.intro: She closes the notebook and looks at the page of ticks. She: "Not enough. But you answered honestly about the ones you love, and that is worth something." She tucks a pressed leaf into your hand and goes back to her tea.

success.text: The leaf smells faintly of mint. She waves you on without looking up.

effects.text: The Trivia Mentor quizzed you about your own journey

remembers.intro: She closes the notebook and looks at the page of ticks. She: "Enough. You know your own road. Now choose what to remember." She opens the notebook to a page so old the ink is brown, three moves written on it.

success.text: She rests two fingers on your lead's brow and hums a few notes of something very old. When she steps back, your lead knows Counter, a move tutors stopped teaching before you were born. She: "Nobody remembers it. Now somebody does."

effects.text: The Trivia Mentor taught your lead Counter
